# 1 Enoch Chapter 94 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Ge'ez MS; cf. 4QEn (Aramaic) | **Section:** Epistle of Enoch — Woe Oracles

---

**1** So now, my sons: love righteousness and live by it. The paths of righteousness lead somewhere worth going — they are accepted and honored. But the paths of unrighteousness will be suddenly swept away. Gone.

**2** For some people in every generation, the roads of violence and death will be laid wide open before them. Stay far away from those roads. Don't follow them.

**3** Hear me, you who are righteous: don't walk on the paths of wickedness. Don't walk on the paths of death. Don't even get close — or you'll be destroyed along with them.

**4** Instead: seek righteousness. Choose a life that is truly chosen by God. Walk the paths of peace. If you do, you will live, and you will flourish.

**5** Keep my words alive in your hearts — don't let them be wiped away. I know what sinners will do: they will work to corrupt wisdom, to drive her out, to leave no room for her anywhere.

**6** Woe to those who build their empires on injustice and oppression, who lay deceit as their cornerstone — they will be suddenly torn down, and they will never know peace.

**7** Woe to those who build their houses on sin — from the foundation up, they will be toppled, and they will fall by the sword. Every person who hoards gold and silver will perish swiftly in the day of judgment.

**8** Woe to you, the wealthy — you who have banked everything on your riches. You will lose every bit of it. And the reason is this: you never once thought of the Most High in all your prosperous days.

**9** You have blasphemed. You have done wrong. You have made yourselves ripe for the day of slaughter — the day of darkness, the day of the great reckoning.

**10** Hear this clearly: the One who made you will be the one who tears you down. There will be no mercy for your ruin. Your own Creator will take satisfaction in your destruction.

**11** In those days, even the righteous among you will be an embarrassment to sinners — a living reproach to the godless.

---

*PNEUMA notes: This chapter ignites the fire of the Epistle. The woe oracles here are not warnings — they are verdicts. The wealthy have already condemned themselves. V. 10 is one of the most shocking verses in all of 1 Enoch: God takes pleasure in the destruction of those who built their lives on exploitation. Compare James 5:1–6, which appears to draw directly on this tradition.*
